kind: EncryptionConfig

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical security tooling integration and explains how to enforce image signing early.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing with cosign
- Manifest parsing to collect images
- CI integration (GitHub Actions) and local validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PUBKEY=${COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY:-cosign.pub}
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  images=$(yq e '.. | .image? // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  for img in $images; do
    cosign verify --key "$PUBKEY" "$img" || { echo "Unsigned: $img"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dynamic image tags vs. digests in this gate?
- How would you test the workflow locally before opening a PR?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RuntimePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-runtime-policy
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    namespaces: ["tenant-a-*"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you manage updates to PolicyStore and revoke exceptions?
- How would you measure policy evaluation latency at scale?

## Why This Is Asked

- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
# OPA policy (partial) enforcing CVE threshold and SBOM signing

default allow = false
allow {
  input.images[_].cve_score <= 6.0
  input.images[_].sbom_signed
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Assess mastery of reproducible builds, attestation, SBOMs, and supply chain controls in CI/CD for a multi-service repo.

## Key Concepts

- Reproducible builds, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
- Image signing with cosign and attestation
- SBOM generation with Syft and verification against digest
- Monorepo with multiple languages and per-service artifacts

## Code Example

```yaml
name: Repro Build Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build deterministically
        run: |
          export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD)
          docker buildx build --build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --tag $IMAGE .
      - name: Sign image
        run: cosign sign $IMAGE
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft packages docker://${IMAGE} -o spdx
      - name: Verify
        run: cosign verify --signature public.key --certificate-identity-id "monorepo" $IMAGE
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate cosign keys and SBOM verification keys?
- How do you handle caching and parallelization in a large mono-repo?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical policy-as-code skills and integration of admission controls into CI for a multi-cloud, large-scale platform.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- securityContext runAsNonRoot and runAsUser
- privileged and capabilities.drop
- hostPath/hostIPC/hostPID prohibition
- CI validation with kubectl/dry-run and Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (high-level sketch)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sprivilege
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sPrivilege
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8sprivilege
      violation["privilege violation"] {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
      }
```
```yaml
# Failing manifest (hostPath & privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
            runAsNonRoot: false
            runAsUser: 0
            capabilities:
              drop: []
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /tmp
            type: Directory
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest (non-root, restricted caps, no hostPath)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            privileged: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
      volumes: []
```

- Run Gatekeeper in CI and verify failing/passing manifests via kubectl apply --dry-run and gatekeeper playbooks.
- Confirm PRs fail on bad manifests and pass on good manifests.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to translate policy requirements into a practical CI gate and runtime checks across multi-tenant clusters.

## Key Concepts

- Image digest pinning and registry scoping
- imagePullSecrets for private registries
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for manifest validation
- Test manifests and CI verification steps

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy skeleton
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-digest-private-registry
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: digest-required
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "DaemonSet", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Images must reference a digest and use private registry with imagePullSecrets."
      pattern:
        spec.template.spec.containers[].image: '*@sha256:*'
```

```yaml
# Example compliant manifest (digest present, private registry)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: reg-creds
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: private.registry.example.com/app@sha256:1111aaaa2222bbbb3333cccc4444dddd5555eeee6666
```

## Follow-up Questions
